comment: A profile is model x quant x platform x config. The id a user types carries no platform -- the CLI detects it -- so each id holds one record per platform under `variants`, and every record states its own platform. Ids follow <model>-<quant>-<gpus>. Quant tags: xxs=IQ2_XXS(-Q2_K), q4ktail=Q4K-tail, mxfp4=MXFP4, q4k=Q4_K, q2k=Q2_K, q2kxl=UD-Q2_K_XL, nvfp4=NVFP4.

glm52-vision.title: GLM-5.2-Vision
glm52-vision.shared_note: The mmproj is found by globbing the text GGUF's directory and its parent, so it must sit at the repo root while the shards live in antirez-routed/.

IQ2_XXS.title: UD-IQ2_XXS_RoutedIQ2XXS_blk78Q2K
IQ2_XXS.summary: Maximum throughput and longest context. Noticeably weaker at reasoning and precise transcription; fine for classification, routing, short summarization.

Q2_K.title: UD-Q2_K_RoutedQ2K
Q2_K.summary: The tuned path, and what the published throughput numbers were measured on. Best quality that still fits two MI300X with a large KV pool.

Q4_K.title: UD-Q4_K_RoutedQ4K
Q4_K.summary: Reach for this when the task is precision-sensitive: multi-step tool use, code, math, or reading small text out of images. Quantization error compounds across reasoning steps in a way it does not in summarization.

speculator.note: DSpark draft. Speculation costs quality nothing -- the verifier accepts or rejects every draft token -- so it is on by default.

dsv4-flash.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
dsv4-flash.shared_note: Text only -- this model has no vision tower, so there is no projector to fetch.

speculator.note: Pinned DSpark/DFlash drafter built for the 0731 verifier. Its published DSpark block size is 5, and its draft KV uses TurboQuant.

MXFP4.title: MXFP4Experts (0731)
MXFP4.summary: The tuned path. Routed experts in OCP MXFP4, served through the native GGUF quantized kernels, and the smaller of the two four-GPU builds.

Q4_K.title: Q4KExperts (0731)
Q4_K.summary: Highest quality of the four, imatrix. Every non-expert tensor is identical to the MXFP4 build; only the routed experts differ.

Q4K-tail.title: Layers37-42Q4KExperts (0731)
Q4K-tail.summary: Q4_K on the last six expert layers, IQ2_XXS gate/up with Q2_K down on the rest. Fits two GPUs while keeping the layers nearest the output at higher precision.

IQ2_XXS.title: IQ2XXS-w2Q2K (0731)
IQ2_XXS.summary: Smallest. IQ2_XXS gate/up experts with Q2_K down. On Metal, measured grouped vector MoE is faster than the padded per-expert tile alternative; ROCm and Ampere use native grouped tile paths (A100 pairs gate/up, SwiGLU, and Q8_1 emission before native Q2_K down).

kimi-k3.title: Kimi K3
kimi-k3.shared_note: The vision projector is not in antirez's text repo; it comes from unsloth/Kimi-K3-GGUF. BF16 is preferred because the source vision weights are BF16.

speculator.note: The exact 64-head draft is tensor-sharded at TP8. At TP6 its five-layer backbone is replicated per rank because neither 64 attention heads nor its width divide by six; vocabulary logits remain distributed.

IQ2_XXS-Q2_K.title: Kimi-K3-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K
IQ2_XXS-Q2_K.summary: The only published quant: IQ2_XXS gate/up experts with Q2_K down. 896 routed experts, 93 layers, 24 MLA + 69 KDA.

patch.why: The published file sets kimi-k3.vision = false, which is wrong: the model has a vision tower and the loader skips it otherwise.

assembly.note: Concatenate in lexical order, then apply the patch. Needs 799 GiB free on top of the parts unless the parts are removed as it goes.

qwen38-27b.title: Qwen3.8-27B
qwen38-27b.shared_note: The mmproj vision tower is discovered by globbing mmproj* next to the text GGUF, so both live in the repo root of the local dir.

q2kxl.title: Unsloth dynamic Q2_K_XL (UD, per-layer mixed)
q2kxl.summary: Unsloth dynamic 2-bit build; the campaign target quant.

speculator.note: DFlash 2 drafter (Inco AI, 2026-08-18): 5-layer qwen3-classed block-diffusion drafter reading target layers [5, 19, 33, 47, 61], trained with block size 8, with a top-16 path selector (rank-256 bilinear over adjacent candidates) and two-tap dynamic convolutions around every sublayer. Vendor-measured mean acceptance 4.80 at block 8; the Metal profile uses the first 3 draft positions because its M=4 verify kernel is faster on both retained text arms than verifying all 7 drafts. Re-blessed 2026-08-25: z-lab republished the file (1,143,006,752 -> 1,143,006,816 B) to fix an off-by-one in dflash.target_layers, which are 1-based in the GGUF and converted with layer-1 at load. The old file stored [5, 19, 33, 47, 61] and therefore read target layers [4, 18, 32, 46, 60] -- one lower than intended; the new file stores [6, 20, 34, 48, 62] and reads the documented [5, 19, 33, 47, 61]. Verified by reading the republished file's metadata, not by trusting the upload: 5 blocks, block size 8, SWA 2048, 32/8 heads at 128, hidden 5120, selector rank 256 top-16, two-tap conv (group 16), mask token 248070.

qwen38-flash-next-fp8.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
qwen38-flash-next-fp8.shared_note: Safetensors checkpoint served from its directory; the vision tower, MTP drafter and processor configs ship in the same repo.

FP8.title: FP8 (block-128 MoE experts, BF16 backbone)
FP8.summary: The official release: 512-expert MoE weights in block-128 FP8, everything else (GDN, QSA, hyper-connections, embeddings, vision tower) BF16, plus 47.7 GiB of FP8 n-gram embedding shards designed for host-memory offload.

metal.title: Apple Silicon (Metal)
metal.why_gate_is_memory: A Mac is one device with one pool, so counting GPUs says nothing about whether a model fits. Weights, KV and activations all come out of unified memory, and the ceiling that matters is what Metal will let the GPU hold, not what the box advertises.
notes: Metal caps a single MTLBuffer well below total memory -- 80.6 GiB of 128 GiB on an M5 Max. The GGUF loader avoids a file-sized buffer by materializing tensors as separate MPS allocations.
recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize is roughly 90% of physical (115.4 of 128 GiB measured on an M5 Max). The min_memory_bytes figures are physical RAM, chosen to leave that margin plus a KV pool.
No multi-device story: Apple exposes one GPU per machine, so every Metal profile is tensor_parallel_size 1 and scaling past one box means separate machines.

rtx3090.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
notes: GeForce driver disables GPU peer-to-peer, so every tensor-parallel collective stages through host memory. Profiles on this platform should prefer expert parallelism and host-offloaded tables over designs that add per-step all-reduces.
SM86 has no FP8 tensor cores; FP8 checkpoints serve through the Marlin W8A16 weight-only kernels.

glm52-q2k-2.summary: The tuned configuration. Leaves six GPUs free for other work.

glm52-xxs-1.summary: Single Apple Silicon machine, sized by unified memory rather than card count. Needs 256 GB for IQ2_XXS and 512 GB for Q2_K or Q4_K.
glm52-xxs-1.status_reason: GLM-shaped sparse MLA has not been validated on Metal
glm52-xxs-1.status_detail: DeepSeek-V4 now has a measured Metal path, but the separate GLM-shaped sparse-MLA and vision path remains unvalidated. The CLI keeps this profile gated until that model is exercised end to end.

notes: Not yet runnable: this model serves through sparse MLA, and the Metal sparse-MLA kernels do not exist yet. These engine settings are starting points chosen to fit the memory budget, not measured configurations -- unlike every other profile in this file.
Metal has no CUDA-graph equivalent, so graph capture is disabled through compilation_config.

max_num_seqs is deliberately small. Batched serving is the weakest part of every Metal engine surveyed -- ds4 still runs attention and routed experts per session -- so concurrency here is a guess, not a tested ceiling.
DSpark is enabled, with TurboQuant attention and a turboquant_k8v4 draft KV cache.
Q2_K and Q4_K need a 512 GB Mac Studio. IQ2_XXS is the only quant a 256 GB machine can hold.

k3-xxs-6.title: Kimi K3 on 6 GPUs
k3-xxs-6.summary: Tensor parallel across six cards; TP4 does not fit. Two GPUs stay free, and this remains the measured low-concurrency reference while k3-xxs-8 has the highest measured throughput at concurrency 8.

notes: The Kimi verifier keeps its native hybrid cache at auto. The replicated DSpark backbone uses a separate TurboQuant compressed cache on every rank.

The exact draft's 64 query heads, 16 KV heads and 14336 intermediate width do not divide by six. SlimServe therefore replicates the five-layer draft backbone and its small quantized Markov head on each rank; target weights and base vocabulary logits remain distributed.

Target CUDA graphs are disabled for speculative KDA decode: full-decode graphs are not supported for this stateful path, and ROCm piecewise capture can terminate a worker during startup. The DSpark draft graphs are disabled separately.
HSA_XNACK=1 is required for this load.

reasoning_parser must be kimi_k3. K3 frames every channel in XTML rather than with <think>, and the generation prompt opens the first channel, so the parser has to start inside it and drop the closing frame. Under any other parser the answer arrives with "<|close|> response <|sep|> <|close|> message <|sep|>" attached, or -- in thinking mode -- lands entirely in reasoning.

k3-xxs-8.title: Kimi K3 on 8 GPUs
k3-xxs-8.summary: All eight cards on every request: attention tensor-parallel at 12 heads per rank, experts held whole and split 112-per-rank. Expert parallelism is required -- tensor-sharding the experts slices GGUF quant blocks at TP8.

notes: kv_cache_dtype must be 'auto': this fork defaults the cache to fp8 for GLM. fp8 loads and answers correctly here but is a net loss, because K3 is a hybrid. Attention pages must be at least as large as the fixed KDA state page, so halving the per-token attention KV doubles the attention block size (960 -> 1920 tokens) to reach the same page size, and every sequence rounds up to that. Measured on TP6: 344,746 cache tokens and 42.1x concurrency at auto, versus 205,824 and 25.1x at fp8_e4m3.
HSA_XNACK=1 is required for this load.

Target CUDA graphs are disabled for speculative KDA decode: full-decode graphs are not supported for this stateful path, and ROCm piecewise capture can terminate a worker during startup. The DSpark draft graphs are disabled separately.

reasoning_parser must be kimi_k3. K3 frames every channel in XTML rather than with <think>, and the generation prompt opens the first channel, so the parser has to start inside it and drop the closing frame. Under any other parser the answer arrives with "<|close|> response <|sep|> <|close|> message <|sep|>" attached, or -- in thinking mode -- lands entirely in reasoning.

dsv4-xxs-1.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash IQ2_XXS on 1 GPU / Apple Silicon
dsv4-xxs-1.summary: Text only. The smallest 0731 target and its matching DSpark drafter run on one MI300X or a 128 GiB Apple Silicon machine.

notes: block_size must be 256: the DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA backend rejects GLM's 64 with 'no common block size'.
sparse_mla_force_mqa is required, or short prompts take a dense forward the ROCm sparse backend does not implement.
Context comes from the GGUF (1M, yarn over a 65536 base); KV is sized by the default utilization rather than a measured byte budget.
reasoning_parser must be set: this fork defaults it to glm45 for its GLM target, and that parser classifies a whole DeepSeek reply as reasoning, leaving content null for every API client.
Measured on an Apple M5 Max with the IQ2_XXS target, the matching 0731 DSpark drafter, and a TurboQuant k8v4 draft cache.
block_size must be 256 so the target compressor, sparse MLA, and draft cache share compatible pages.
reasoning_parser must be set, or the GLM default classifies a whole DeepSeek reply as reasoning and leaves content null.

The 16 GiB hybrid KV pool is a ceiling, not a promise: it holds one full 262,144-token request (target fp8_ds_mla across 43 layers plus the 3-layer TurboQuant draft cache, ~9 GiB) with margin for concurrent shorter sessions, and the Metal worker shrinks it to whatever stays resident on the machine it boots on. Sizing it from artifact bytes is what broke on 2026-08-25: 80.8 GiB target + 6.5 GiB drafter looks like 87.3 GiB but loads to 93.57 GiB, and an M5 Max's Metal working set is 107.52 GiB rather than the ~115 GiB assumed here, so the pool overran the working set and served token soup at 1.1 tok/s. On that machine the worker now grants ~9.6 GiB. Higher API concurrency drains in scheduler waves instead of paging model weights.
max_model_len is 262144 for real (agentic) use. The 1k-in/2k-out benchmark matrix in perf/baseline_status.md is re-gated under this sizing (see the M1 Ultra campaign entries).

max_num_batched_tokens is 2176 = 2048 + 32 seqs x 4 speculative slots: the scheduler reserves draft-token room, so 2048 would cap scheduled prefill tokens at 1920 and split a 2048-token prompt into two chunks (measured ~230 ms scheduler boundary plus an inefficient 128-token tail chunk).

Long-context status (2026-08-23): the sparse-MLA indexer chain (fused indexer Q rope/quant, prefill top-k, scoring) has a native Metal implementation. Async output copies and their completion event stay on the producing MPS stream (unit-tested), which is believed to remove the cold cross-stream event ordering failure; the deterministic cold-boot wedge repro (primer then a direct multi-chunk prefill) has not been re-run, so the boot-ramp protocol in perf/prefill_handoff.md remains the ops guidance until it is. Prefill top-k sizes native work from the active request window and streams windows above 1,024 candidates with fixed scratch; the 65,536-candidate native oracle matches the eager chain on tie ordering and the streaming loop (its all-zero-query block does not exercise scoring). Full 262,144-token end-to-end serving still needs a dedicated long-context validation pass.

TP4 x DP2 measured 111 c1 / 118-271 hot c8 for MXFP4 and was rejected. For maximum aggregate throughput see dsv4-q4ktail-8.

dsv4-q4k-8.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash Q4_K on 8 GPUs
dsv4-q4k-8.summary: Text only. Eight-way tensor parallelism with the highest-quality 0731 Q4_K target by default.

notes: block_size must be 256: the DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA backend rejects GLM's 64 with 'no common block size'.
sparse_mla_force_mqa is required, or short prompts take a dense forward the ROCm sparse backend does not implement.
Context comes from the GGUF (1M, yarn over a 65536 base); KV is sized by the default utilization rather than a measured byte budget.
reasoning_parser must be set: this fork defaults it to glm45 for its GLM target, and that parser classifies a whole DeepSeek reply as reasoning, leaving content null for every API client.

qwen38-nvfp4-1.title: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on 1 GPU
qwen38-nvfp4-1.summary: Vision-language 27B hybrid (gated-deltanet linear attention, 1-in-4 full attention) on a single MI300X. 23 GiB of weights leave most of the card for KV and linear-attention state.

notes: NVFP4 MLP weights decode through the ROCm emulation NVFP4 linear kernel (gfx942 has no FP4 hardware); the FP8 tensors use the native MI300X FP8 path. A native gfx942 NVFP4 decode kernel is an open optimization, not a blocker.

linear_backend must be auto, not this fork's aiter default: the aiter filter leaves no NVFP4 kernel at all, and the aiter FP8 scaled-mm kernels refuse this model's untuned GEMM shapes (e.g. the 16384x5120 GDN qkvz projection). Auto keeps aiter where its tuned configs exist and falls back elsewhere; tuning the Qwen3.8 FP8 shapes in aiter is the follow-up optimization. Both the top-level flag and kernel_config.linear_backend must be set: the top-level flag defaults to aiter and overwrites the kernel_config value whenever it is not auto.
kv_cache_dtype must be 'auto': this fork defaults the cache to fp8 for its GLM target, and the hybrid GDN/full-attention cache has only been validated at auto here.

FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph capture (size 64) is qualified for this hybrid GDN + MTP path and is a measured 1.4x at c1: unlike Kimi's KDA, the qwen GDN decode captures cleanly on ROCm. Capture 64 covers the c8 spec verify width.

NVFP4 layers run the vendored QuixiCore HIP kernels (RocmNativeNvFp4LinearKernel): decode-width calls (M<=4, the c1 spec-verify size) read the packed E2M1 weight directly through the q8 dp4a GEMV (measured 1.3-1.8x per layer), wider batches use a load-time-dequantized bf16 copy through hipBLASLt (~22 GiB extra weights memory) until the MFMA packed MMQ exists. VLLM_NVFP4_TRITON_GEMM=0 falls back to the emulation kernel, whose own load-time cache is controlled by VLLM_NVFP4_EMULATION_CACHE_WEIGHTS.

reasoning_parser must be qwen3 and tool_call_parser qwen3_xml: the template thinks in <think> blocks and calls tools with <function=...> XML; the fork's glm45/glm47 defaults would classify whole replies as reasoning and miss tool calls.
Speculation uses the checkpoint's own qwen3_5_mtp drafter rather than a separate DSpark artifact; there is no TurboQuant draft KV here because the drafter shares the target's cache layout.

max_cudagraph_capture_size raised 64->192 to satisfy the capture-coupling rule (>= (k+1) x max_num_seqs at MTP k=2, seqs 64): with 64, decode batches above 21 requests silently ran eager (measured on rtx3090 as a -52% cliff before its fix). Raise is safety-directional (more graphs, same kernels); MI300X re-baseline pending.

muse-kdyn-1.title: Muse-Glimmer-30B on one Mac
muse-kdyn-1.summary: Vision-language 28B dense model on a single Apple Silicon machine, sized by unified memory. Full 131072-token context; both published k-quants fit a 64 GB Mac.

notes: Interleaved attention: 3 sliding-window (2048) layers per 1 global layer across 52 layers, GQA 32/2, final logit softcapping 20. The hybrid KV manager caps SWA layers at the window, so the 12 GiB pool covers multiple full-context requests on the 13 global layers.
Vision: 50-block CLIP tower at 896 px, patch 14, 2x2 spatial merge into 6656-dim tokens, loaded from the published mmproj GGUF.
DFlash speculation is on by default: the drafter proposes one 16-token block per call against target layers [2, 14, 26, 38, 50].

reasoning_parser must be muse_glimmer: replies use '<|start|>assistant to=self<|message|>...' self-segments, and the fork's glm45 default would classify the whole reply as reasoning, leaving content null.
tool_call_parser must be muse_glimmer: tool calls use the model's native ATEM recipient/invoke/parameter envelope, including Responses custom-tool payloads.
kv_cache_dtype must be auto (bf16): this fork defaults the KV cache to fp8_e4m3, and the Metal dense/GQA backend has no fp8 KV path.

Performance note (2026-08-15): DFlash speculation (always on) measures 19.9-20.1 tok/s rested on the 256-token greedy essay bench (fused verify step + tensor-ops kernels on the M5 GPU neural accelerators), ahead of plain fused decode (14.4-16.4); long-context (10k, cached decode) 11.0. Acceptance ~1.73/draft. See perf/baseline_status.md. llama.cpp reference on this box: 26.75 plain / 30.8 spec; vendor ExecuTorch 26.6/50.2.

qwen38-q2kxl-1.title: Qwen3.8-27B on one Mac
qwen38-q2kxl-1.summary: Vision-language 27B hybrid-attention model on a single Apple Silicon machine, sized by unified memory. Unsloth dynamic Q2_K_XL fits a 48 GB Mac with a 12 GiB KV pool.

notes: Hybrid attention (qwen3_5): 64 text layers in a 3:1 interleave -- 48 gated-deltanet linear-attention layers (16 K-heads/48 V-heads at 128 dim, conv kernel 4) and 16 full-attention layers (GQA 24/4, head_dim 256, partial rotary 0.25, interleaved MRoPE). Only the 16 full layers hold paged KV; the rest carry recurrent state, which is why prefix caching is off.

Vision: the shared Qwen3.5 tower (27 blocks at hidden 1152, patch 16, 2x2 spatial merge into 5120-dim tokens), loaded from the published mmproj-F16 GGUF. GGUF and safetensors artifacts share one model implementation; the GGUF adapter restores the Conv3d patch-embed layout llama.cpp splits into two taps, and the processor is synthesized from the mmproj metadata.

DFlash 2 speculation is on by default: the drafter evaluates the first 3 draft positions of its trained 8-token block against target layers [5, 19, 33, 47, 61], keeps top-16 candidates per position, and walks one path via the rank-256 selector. The shorter Metal verify width is measured faster than all 7 drafts on both essay and GSM8K-style arms; rejection sampling keeps the target distribution unchanged.
kv_cache_dtype must be auto (bf16): this fork defaults the KV cache to fp8_e4m3, and the Metal backends have no fp8 KV path.
max_model_len 131072 of the model's 262144: matched to the muse profile until the hybrid KV/state manager is measured on Metal.

qwen38fn-fp8-8.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 on 8 GPUs
qwen38fn-fp8-8.summary: Vision-language 125B-A6B hybrid (Gated DeltaNet + Qwen Sparse Attention, 1-in-4 full attention, 4-branch gated residual) with 51B n-gram embeddings held in pinned host memory. FP8 experts run expert-parallel through Marlin W8A16 on 8x RTX 3090.

notes: enable_expert_parallel is a correctness requirement, not a tuning choice: moe_intermediate_size is 640 and the FP8 block scales are [128, 128], so a TP shard of 80 cannot carry exact block scales. EP keeps 64 whole experts per rank (640 = 5 x 128).

moe_backend and linear_backend must be auto, not this fork's aiter defaults: AITER kernels do not exist on CUDA, and the forced-backend path raises at load ('FP8 MoE backend AITER does not support ... device cuda'). Both the top-level flags and kernel_config must be set, since a non-auto top-level flag overwrites kernel_config (same rule the qwen38-nvfp4-1 MI300X profile documents for linear_backend).
SM86 has no FP8 tensor cores and Triton FP8 MoE requires SM89+, so the experts run the Marlin W8A16 block-FP8 MoE kernels (weight-only decode to BF16 compute).

VLLM_QWEN4_EXP_PLE_HOST=1 keeps the full 47.7 GiB n-gram (PLE) table pinned in host RAM per rank and gathers the 16 rows per token (2560 bytes) from the GPU over UVA inside the forward, exactly as the model card intends ('tables prefetched from host memory'). The gather is graph-capturable, so FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture keeps working, and the TP-replicated table removes the per-step embedding all-reduce that this no-P2P platform cannot afford. Host cost: ~48 GiB pinned per rank (~382 GiB total of the 996 GiB box).

Multi-GPU GeForce runs fine on the stock NVIDIA driver but leaves 36-58% of TP throughput on the table: install QuixiAI's P2P driver (github.com/QuixiAI/open-gpu-kernel-modules, see docs/geforce-p2p.md) for direct GPU-GPU DMA. Measured on this profile: c1 109.6->148.8 (+36%), c8 409.7->647.9 (+58%). NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS in this env is required for P2P across root complexes and harmless on stock drivers.
reasoning_parser qwen3 and tool_call_parser qwen3_xml: the template thinks in <think> blocks and calls tools with <function=...> XML.
Speculation uses the checkpoint's own single-layer QSA MTP drafter (Qwen4ExpMTP) via method 'mtp'; there is no separate DSpark artifact for this model yet.

max_model_len is the model's native 262144, enabled by VLLM_QWEN4_EXP_TQ_MAIN_KV=1: the main QSA KV is stored as TurboQuant k8v4 (fp8 keys + 4-bit values, per-slot f16 scale/zero, 2.64x smaller than bf16), decoded in-register by the sparse-gather kernel. Measured cost vs bf16@131072 is within noise at c8-c32 and ~8% at c1; draft acceptance stays at bf16 parity. bf16 KV cannot fit 262144 on 24 GiB cards (weights take 17.6 GiB).

max_num_seqs 32 with max_cudagraph_capture_size 96: at MTP k=2 every decode step is seqs x 3 query tokens, so 96 covers full-batch decode steps with FULL graphs (c32 measured 425 tok/s eager vs 880 graphed). Raising max_num_seqs requires raising the capture size with it (3 x max_num_seqs) or the largest batches silently run eager.
The QSA sparse-gather kernel pins narrow tiles (block_n 16, 4 warps) for quantized KV: the wide-tile profile that suits bf16 collapses in-register dequant 3.8x (TQ) to 23x (fp8) at 48+ token steps.

min_host_ram_bytes gates this platform at 128 GiB system RAM: the 47.7 GiB n-gram (PLE) table is pinned ONCE in a /dev/shm segment shared by all TP ranks (not per rank), plus load staging and runtime headroom. A machine that passes the GPU gate but lacks the RAM fails at plan time instead of dying mid-load.

Dynamic speculative decoding is supported and measured: adding 'num_speculative_tokens': 3 and 'num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size': [[1,4,3],[5,32,2]] to speculative_overrides (with max_cudagraph_capture_size 128) buys +19.5% at concurrency 4 for -2.6% at concurrency 32 (824 vs 846 tok/s, fully explained by k=3 ramp/drain acceptance). Static k=2 stays the default because c32 is this profile's peak; flip the overrides for latency-shaped traffic. The V2 runner captures one uniform-decode graph family per scheduled k, clipped to each k's batch range.
